issues.description: The proposal fabricates highly specific details not found in the Client Matrix, including '$85M (2025 revenue)', 'Columbus, OH', '200 employees', '40 dispatchers', '600 contracted drivers', and '7-year-old custom Ruby on Rails 5 application maintained internally by 2 engineers'. Stating unverified information as fact is a critical failure.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove all hallucinated demographic, financial, and technical specifics. Only include details explicitly provided in the Client Matrix.

issues.description: The proposal omits a high-confidence risk from the Client Matrix: previous internal attempts to fix the workflow issues have failed twice. This is a meaningful gap that needs to be addressed to show the client we understand their history.
issues.suggested_fix: Acknowledge the two previous failed internal attempts in the Understanding section and briefly note in the Approach how the proposed methodology will avoid a similar outcome.

issues.description: The proposal mentions the ELD compliance deadline but fails to include the high-confidence business impact of missing it: potential fines or loss of operating authority.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the Strategic Context to explicitly mention that failure to meet ELD compliance could result in fines or loss of operating authority.

risks: The inclusion of fabricated company and technical details severely undermines the firm's credibility and would be highly embarrassing if presented to the client.

While the proposal correctly flags the Q3 vs Q4 pilot timeline as an open question, structuring the entire Phase & Timeline section around a 'Targeted Q3 Pilot' might alienate the CTO before alignment is reached.
